group_assessment.counts_measured: PubMed esearch 2026-10-03 (tool=LEGEND-research): 'Chang NS[au]' 138, 'Chang NS[au] AND WWOX' 66, 'Hsu LJ[au]' 103, 'Hsu LJ[au] AND WWOX' 30.
group_assessment.weighting: Five of the six papers in this group come from one laboratory lineage (Chang N-S / Hsu L-J, National Cheng Kung University). That laboratory originated WWOX and carries the gene's largest single output, so its measurements carry full weight; what it does NOT carry is independence. Two of its subjects are exclusive to it: 'Zfra NOT Chang NS[au]' returns 1 record and that record is an unrelated zebrafish androgen-receptor paper matching the string by accident; 'TIAF1 NOT Chang NS[au]' returns 5 of 20. The autophagy axis is the opposite case and is the reason this group is readable as a contradiction at all: 'WWOX AND autophagy' returns 10 records and 8 of them are from neither Chang NS nor Hsu LJ.
group_assessment.note: Research-group knowledge base is excluded from the public edition; this rests on measured PubMed counts and on the papers' own author lists.

field_density.note: WWOX is a named subject, but this is a perspective review: no experiment is performed in it.

multihop.enumeration_method: 112 <ref> elements, 113 PMIDs in the deposit. Two references were resolved by hand because they bear directly on the group's assigned question; the remaining bibliography was not classified.

resolved.why: Reference 31 - 'WWOX promotes apoptosis and inhibits autophagy in paclitaxel-treated ovarian carcinoma cells'. A SECOND laboratory reporting the same sign as PMID 24008736, which changes the independence structure of the contradiction this group was built around.

Reference 101 - 'WWOX inhibition by Zfra1-31 restores mitochondrial homeostasis and viability of neuronal cells exposed to high glucose'. An independent laboratory, a NEURONAL system, and the same sign as PMID 41677633: removing WWOX function protects the mitochondrion.

multihop.dedup_performed: The two resolved PMIDs were checked with registry_records.py: 33300063 is carried as CORPUS-STUB-056 (not_processed); 35984507 was not reached by the queries run here.

corpus_crossquery.query: What does the corpus already carry for this review, and does it record the hierarchy claim?
corpus_crossquery.finding: CORPUS-STUB-010 and LIT-0037 carry the identity; DL-MOL-006 carries the Zfra peptide axis. Nothing in the registries records that the 'overrides' relation is asserted by a review with no head-to-head experiment, which is the single fact a reader needs before treating Zfra and WWOX restoration as ranked alternatives.

verbatim_locators.note: Coverage: abstract, all eleven numbered sections, concluding remarks and the reference list. Figure legends read. This article has no supplement.

entries.proposition: THE HIERARCHY IS ASSERTED IN THE SUMMARY OF A PERSPECTIVE REVIEW, NOT MEASURED. The word 'determined' appears without an accompanying experiment in this article, which performs none; the three routes it then lists are mechanisms, not a comparison of two therapeutic arms.
entries.snippet: We determined that Zfra overrides WWOX in suppressing cancer growth and the progression of neurodegeneration.
entries.anchor: Section 11, 'Summary and Concluding Remarks', second sentence

entries.proposition: THE SAME ARTICLE STATES THE SAME RELATION CONDITIONALLY TWO PARAGRAPHS LATER. The two sentences are the range of what this source supports; a model that carries only the first has carried the stronger half of a hedge.
entries.snippet: Zfra may override WWOX deficiency in restoring normal physiological functions.

entries.proposition: THE ONE GENOTYPE-LEVEL ORGANELLE-ADJACENT DATUM CITED HERE IS A HETEROZYGOTE FINDING, and it is cited, not shown. A heterozygous mouse cortex is the closest this review comes to a WWOX dose model, and the finding is an aggregation phenotype, not an organelle endpoint.
entries.snippet: A recent intriguing discovery is that pT12-WWOX occurs as aggregates in the cortex of heterozygous Wwox mice, but not in wild-type mice
entries.anchor: Section 11.1, 'pT12-WWOX as an Initiator of Protein Aggregation Cascade?', second sentence

entries.proposition: THE REVIEW CARRIES, FROM AN INDEPENDENT LABORATORY AND A NEURONAL SYSTEM, THE SAME DIRECTION AS THE LYSOSOME PAPER: INHIBITING WWOX PROTECTS THE MITOCHONDRION. Activated WWOX is presented as the agent of mitochondrial apoptosis under a metabolic stress, which is the direction a WWOX-restoration strategy has to answer.
entries.snippet: WWOX becomes Y33-phosphorylated in response to high glucose, which leads to mitochondrial apoptosis.
entries.anchor: Section 10.3, 'Zfra1-31 for Treating Hyperglycemia/Diabetes-Associated Neurodegeneration', second paragraph
